title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 24 (Power of Securities and Exchange Board to regulate issue and transfer of securities, etc.)

content.overview: Section 24 allocates administration of specified Companies Act provisions. The provisions contained in Chapter III, Chapter IV and in section 127 shall, in so far as they relate to issue and transfer of securities and non-payment of dividend, be administered by the Securities and Exchange Board of India in the case of listed companies and companies which intend to get their securities listed on any recognised stock exchange in India; and in any other case, by the Central Government. SEBI may exercise powers to call for information, inspect, inquire into, investigate and impose penalties in respect of the matters so administered by it.
content.glance: SEBI administers issue/transfer of securities and non-payment of dividend for listed and intending-to-list companies; Central Government in other cases; SEBI may call for information, inspect, inquire, investigate and levy penalties.
content.study:
Section 24 is an administrative allocation provision.

Statutory test
1. Scope of provisions: Chapter III, Chapter IV and section 127, so far as they relate to (i) issue and transfer of securities and (ii) non-payment of dividend.
2. SEBI field: listed companies and companies which intend to get their securities listed on any recognised stock exchange in India.
3. Central Government residual: any other case.
4. SEBI powers: call for information, inspect, inquire into, investigate and impose penalties in respect of matters administered by it under this section.

Boundary
Section 24 does not repeal or rewrite the substantive Companies Act rules; it assigns who administers them. Unlisted companies that are not intending to list remain with the Central Government for these matters.

sections.heading: SEBI’s allocated field
sections.body: Provisions of Chapter III, Chapter IV and section 127 relating to issue and transfer of securities and non-payment of dividend are administered by SEBI for listed companies and companies which intend to get their securities listed on any recognised stock exchange in India.

sections.heading: Central Government residual role
sections.body: In any other case, those matters are administered by the Central Government.

sections.heading: SEBI’s powers
sections.body: SEBI may call for information, inspect, inquire into, investigate and impose penalties in respect of the matters administered by it under this section.

provisions.title: Power of Securities and Exchange Board to regulate issue and transfer of securities, etc.

examples.title: Listed company dividend default
examples.body: A listed company fails to pay declared dividend. Under section 24 the matter is administered by SEBI.

examples.title: Unlisted company not intending to list
examples.body: An unlisted private company has a dispute about transfer of securities and is not intending to list. Administration remains with the Central Government under section 24.

hypotheticals.question: Does SEBI administer every securities issue under the Companies Act?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 24 allocates specified matters (issue and transfer of securities; non-payment of dividend) for listed companies and companies intending to list; other cases remain with the Central Government.

misconceptions.trap: SEBI replaces the Companies Act for all companies.
misconceptions.correction: Section 24 allocates administration of specified matters; it does not repeal the Companies Act.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 24 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Determine listing status or intention to list. II. Identify whether the matter is issue/transfer of securities or non-payment of dividend under the allocated Chapters/sections. III. Assign SEBI or Central Government. IV. Apply the substantive provision. V. Conclude.
